description: British Commonwealth Air Training Plan Anson rebuilt by the museum's volunteer restoration team from several airframes. Serial unresolved: recorded as RCAF 11567 by Wikipedia and as 886 by silverhawkauthor.
aliases: Anson Mk II; Anson II; Avro 652A

description: CF-100 Mk 5D c/n 376, on outdoor display beside the museum hangar. Also cited as 18476 in early-serial form.
Barkley-Grow T8P-1 c/n 3, a rare twin used on northern Canadian bush routes.
Ex-RCAF Expeditor 3NM 2366, c/n CA-245, later C-FRSX; bought surplus in 1966 by Walter Ross of Lethbridge Air Service.
Beech D18S c/n A-0025, ex-N745PD.
Bell 47G assembled by the museum's volunteer restoration team from a frame and surplus parts under Pat Sauriol's direction.
Bell 206A JetRanger C-FQZB, restored and displayed in the markings of C-GDXC.

Airacobra restoration project in the museum's restoration area; to be finished in the Soviet markings of a Lend-Lease P-39 lost near Wetaskiwin in December 1942. Two P-39 projects are reported on site.
Ex-Pacific Western Airlines Boeing 737-275 recorded on site by Aerial Visuals; silverhawkauthor gives the registration as C-GPIW. Registration transposition unresolved.
CIM-10B Super Bomarc surface-to-air missile displayed inside the museum.

description: Canadair Silver Star, also cited as 21506; carries code PP-506.
Canadair Silver Star c/n T33-533, also cited as 21533, on outdoor display beside the hangar. Wikipedia records the airframe as 21146 marked as 21533; Aerial Visuals reads it as 21533 outright.
The first Canadair Sabre built, c/n 0001, carrying code PX-101.
aliases: Sabre 1; F-86; F86; CL-13; Sabre Mk 1; CL13

description: The airframe is a Lockheed TF-104G bought from a museum in the Netherlands, ex-Royal Netherlands Air Force D-5805, c/n 583E-5805, finished as CF-104D 104651 of 417 Squadron - the aircraft lost near Cold Lake in June 1980 after a bird strike.
aliases: CF104; F-104; F104; Starfighter; D-5805; CF104D

description: DH.60X Cirrus Moth c/n 503, on loan.

Tiger Moth bought by Norman Reid in 1996, flown a further ten years and donated to the museum in 2006. Serial cited variously as RCAF 241, 2114 and (by Aerial Visuals) as FE192 registered C-FCOH; unresolved.

Mosquito B.35 registered CF-HMQ, bought by Bob Campbell and given to the City of Edmonton, which loaned it to the museum. Restored by volunteers to represent a fighter-bomber flown by Russell Bannock. silverhawkauthor gives the serial as VA114; Aerial Visuals and Wikipedia give VP189.
Australian-built Vampire T.35 c/n DHA-4179, later N6528Z. Serial also cited as A79-675.
RCAF Dakota 12927, c/n 13028, later C-FROD.
aliases: CC129; C-47; C47; Dakota; DC-3; DC3

description: Ercoupe c/n 4770; registration cited as CF-FYA by silverhawkauthor and as N39TR by Aerial Visuals, which records the airframe as having left the collection. Presence uncertain.
Fairchild 71C c/n 17, built at the company's Montreal plant from 1929.
Fairchild Argus (UC-61 Forwarder) FK315, later CF-EKK. Recorded on site by Aerial Visuals but not on the museum's public collection pages.
aliases: Argus I; UC-61; UC61; Forwarder; CF-EKK

description: Fleet 80 Canuck c/n 305, donated by the owner's family after his death in 2002.
Fokker Universal bought by Grant McConachie for United Air Transport in 1933 and used to haul fish and miners.
Lockheed Ventura GR Mk V, later CF-FZV. Reported by silverhawkauthor; not on the museum's public collection pages.
aliases: Ventura; PV-1; B-34; Vega V-146; CF-FZV; PV1; B34

description: CF-101B Voodoo c/n 537, on outdoor display beside the hangar. Wikipedia records this airframe as restored in the markings 17425.
Second CF-101B Voodoo on outdoor display; Aerial Visuals reads the site B airframe as c/n 611 with an unresolved serial, silverhawkauthor gives 101060 and Wikipedia 100060.
Norseman IV c/n 94, ex-RCAF 494, later CF-EIH.
aliases: Norseman; UC-64; UC64; Norseman IV; CF-EIH

Gull-wing Stinson SR-9 Reliant.
Waco UIC cabin biplane.

description: Flying replica-scale reproduction of the Canadian Vickers Viking IV amphibian G-CAEB, built by museum volunteers; reported as a 7/8-scale replica.

Accurate replica of the Curtiss Stinson Special flown by Katherine Stinson on her 1917-18 North American tours, built by the museum's volunteer restoration team from archival photographs and Curtiss blueprints.
Curtiss JN-4D restored to flying condition over twenty years by Edmonton airline captain Jack Johnson, flown at airshows until 2009. Also cited with the serial 3793.
One of only three Cranwell CLA.4s built, assembled by members of the Edmonton and Northern Alberta Flying Club.
Replica Fokker D.VIII parasol fighter built by Edmonton pilot Everett Bunnel.

description: Float from the Ford Trimotor CF-BEP only; no airframe. Listed by Wikipedia among the museum's holdings.
